title: Pinning notice templates and operator triage playbook
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc bundles short customer-facing notification templates (activation, partial-fail, rollback) and a concise operator triage playbook for region pin activations. Target audience: SRE/Oncall, Customer Success (CS) leads, Solutions Eng, and Legal when escalations require evidence. Not an exhaustive policy; complements the residency enforcement runbooks (see linked artifacts).

Goals:
- Provide operators a single-file set of scripts/messages for fast, consistent comms during pin changes.
- Define telemetry signals, thresholds, and first-response actions so we reduce mean time to safe-state.
- Offer curated rollback triggers and evidence bundles for audits.

Quick glossary (short):
- Pin: customer region preference that causes routing + storage to keep data in a specified region.
- Soft-pin: preference-driven affinity (best-effort).
- Hard-pin: strict enforcement (request blocked or routed to fallback only if in-region).
- Activation window: scheduled interval when we flip routing rules.

Preconditions before activation (checklist for owner):
- Legal signoff recorded (contract addendum or email thread) — attach to ticket.
- Customer acceptance test (CAT) green for basic L7 flows (see CAT template link in Jira).
- Capacity check: Dedicated pools or region quotas reserved and autoscale policies reviewed.
- Telemetry baseline snapshot captured (last 48h latency, error rates, regional capacity utilization).
- Backup evidence capture enabled (audit logs, routing traces, KV eviction logs).

Activation run steps (operator script):
1) Preflight (T-minus 30 minutes):
   - Post short note to #residency-ops with activation id, customer id, region, expected start, rollback window.
   - Trigger snapshot: /ops/tooling/capture-telemetry --customer $CID --window 48h --tag pre-activation-$ACTID
   - Validate capacity: run /ops/tooling/region-capacity-check --region $REGION --min-gpu 2 --ok-exit-code 0
2) Start (T0):
   - Flip feature flag: /ops/flags flip residency-pin-$CID --to hard --rollout=canary:10%
   - Start canary monitor for 5m: scripts poll the following signals (see telemetry mapping below).
   - Notify CS: DM the customer success lead and send scheduled email (template below).
3) Canary review (T0+10m):
   - If signals OK, increase rollout to 50% for additional 10m, then to 100% if stable.
   - If degraded, hit rollback (see Abort + Rollback).
4) Post-activation (T+1h):
   - Capture post snapshot: /ops/tooling/capture-telemetry --customer $CID --window 60m --tag post-activation-$ACTID
   - Upload evidence bundle to ticket and notify Legal/CS if region pin requires audit trail.

Abort + Rollback (immediate actions if thresholds crossed):
- Abort sequence: flip feature flag back to previous state, route traffic to fallback region, open PagerDuty incident and escalate to oncall.
- Evidence: attach pre/post snapshots, traces for the impacted timeframe, and the routing decision log (required for audit).
- Customer comms: send the "partial-fail" email template immediately and offer a postmortem ETA.

Telemetry mapping (signal name -> what to watch -> threshold -> first response):
- region.latency.p50 (ms): sudden increase > 2x baseline for 5 min -> scale pool if available / investigate network path.
- region.latency.p95 (ms): > baseline + 150ms sustained 5 min -> escalate to oncall and consider rollback.
- region.error_rate.4xx (%) : increase > 1% absolute -> check client contract compatibility and request logs. If new 4xx spikes correlate with pin, push rollback.
- region.error_rate.5xx (%) : > 0.5% absolute for 3 consecutive 1-minute buckets -> auto-abort and rollback.
- kvcache.evictions.per_min: spike > 3x baseline -> investigate memory pressure, consider reduce concurrency or use alternate model variant.
- routing.fallback.rate: > 5% of requests being routed off-pin for > 10m -> engage engineering to inspect routing rules; inform CS.
- backlog.queue.length: > 1000 requests -> scale provisioned capacity or throttle non-critical customers.
- auth.failures.rate: any sustained auth failure > 0.1% -> abort and triage with security.

Operator triage checklist (first 10 minutes):
- Step 0: Acknowledge page and set channel (#residency-ops-<CID>-<ACTID>).
- Step 1: Confirm whether the issue is systemic or pin-specific by comparing global vs region-only signals.
- Step 2: Pull evidence: pre/post telemetry snapshots, routing decision logs for sample request IDs.
- Step 3: If 5xx spike: collect service stack traces, check model process health (OOMs, GPU pre-emption).
- Step 4: If latency spike: verify network metrics (cross-region egress, CDN health), and kernel-level errors.
- Step 5: If routing fallback rate high: check routing table changes and policy engine audit.
- Step 6: Decide: continue rollout / pause / rollback. Document the decision and reasons in the ticket.

Escalation matrix (who to call):
- Oncall SRE (first line): PagerDuty P1 -> handle immediate rollback or mitigation.
- Serving runtime lead: DM / call if kernel/quantization issues suspected.
- Networking(ALB/Cloud infra): page if cross-region egress errors detected.
- Legal/Compliance: notify if customer asks for audit evidence or if retention/region deviation occurs.

Customer notification templates
1) Activation notice (send at T-30 and T0)
Subject: Redwood — Region pin activation for <customer-name> (region: <region>)
Body: Hi <Customer-Owner>,
We plan to activate your region pin to <region> at <time> UTC. Short summary: routing and storage changes will steer requests and new data to the selected region. Expected impact: none for normal usage; short canary windows may cause small latency variation. If you see unexpected errors, please reply here and we will triage immediately.
Best,
Redwood Technical Ops

2) Partial-fail / rollback notice (send immediately if abort)
Subject: Redwood — Temporary rollback during region pin activation for <customer-name>
Body: Hi <Customer-Owner>,
During activation at <time> we observed elevated errors/latency and have temporarily rolled back routing to the previous policy to keep your traffic stable. We are collecting evidence and will share a postmortem within 24 hours. No customer data was moved during the brief window.
Immediate steps we suggest: avoid running mission-critical batch jobs until we confirm stabilization.
Thanks for bearing with us — we will follow up shortly with an incident summary.
Regards,
Redwood Ops (cc: Solutions Eng / CS)
note: Draft; this doc intentionally mixes scripts and human templates. Keep it updated with signal thresholds whenever telemetry baseline changes. Next review planned Q4 2024.
